title: KV cache graceful-trimming: lease-backed prefix retirement and correctness proofs
creator: Alex Moreno
description: Problem: Under continuous batching, large numbers of short-lived prefixes cause high GPU memory pressure. Existing coarse TTL/LRU approaches either evict hot prefixes prematurely or hold cold prefixes too long, causing tail latency and OOM risk. Goal: design and implement a "graceful-trimming" policy for the KV cache that combines prefix-aware leasing, probabilistic TTL windows, and safe retirement proofs so we can reclaim memory without violating correctness (no missing KV entries for in-flight batches).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime supports lease-backed prefix retirement API: acquire/release/renew leases for prefixes under serving runtime.
2) No user-visible correctness regressions: in-flight requests must never observe missing KV keys that would affect generation correctness (measured via regression harness).
3) Memory reduction: 20-30% reduction in average GPU KV footprint for mix-of-short-and-long prefix workloads compared to baseline LRU under production batching traces.
4) Latency SLOs: p99 generation latency increase < 5% on observed workloads after enabling trimming with conservative defaults.
5) End-to-end tests and formal invariants documented and included in CI (unit + integration + chaos tests).
implementation_notes: Overview: implement a lease manager per prefix (lightweight token) that tracks active batch handles referencing the prefix. Trimming marks a prefix candidate for retirement; actual memory reclaim occurs only after lease expiration or explicit verification that no active lease exists.

Trim epochs: worker threads will perform periodic 'trim epochs' where candidates are batched, a compact 'retire token' is signed, and memory reclamation is performed in a single epoch boundary to avoid races with KV readers/writers.
Probabilistic TTL windows: for prefixes with weak access signals, use a short randomized TTL window (jittered 10-30s) to avoid synchronized mass-trims on traffic dips.

Fallbacks: if memory pressure crosses a high-watermark, escalate to aggressive trimming that can preemptively convert low-confidence prefixes into 'evictable' state after a safe fence has been applied (see correctness proofs).

Data structures: maintain per-prefix metadata: last_access_ts, lease_count, candidate_score (hotness heuristic combining recency, frequency, and batch-affinity). Keep this metadata in host memory; only reclaim GPU memory on epoch boundary.
API: expose admin flags to tune jitter, aggressive threshold, and epoch interval. Add metrics for leases_acquired, leases_released, prefixes_retired, prefixes_forced_retirement.
decisions: Lease-based approach chosen over global reference counting to minimize contention and cross-thread synchronization.
Trim epochs chosen to create a single coordination point for safe GPU reclaim, reducing atomic operations during hot paths.
Use probabilistic TTL windows (jitter) to avoid simultaneous retirement storms across workers.
Preserve last-access semantics for prefix affinity scoring but weight batch-affinity higher to prefer keeping prefixes that are frequently co-batched.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease manager: acquire/release/renew under concurrent toy workloads.
Integration test: runtime runs a synthetic continuous-batching trace (mix of 1- to 128-token prefixes) and validates no generation failures and KV consistency.
Chaos test: simulate sudden worker restarts during trim epoch; assert no in-flight requests hit missing KV entries and memory is eventually reclaimed.
Perf experiment: A/B run on perf cluster using production sampling traces for 24h; collect GPU memory histogram, p50/p95/p99 latency, and tokens/sec cost metrics.
Formal check: static invariant proof doc added to repository and a CI job that verifies invariants via model-based tests.
